title.narrative: Integrated emergency response CR-WASH/GBV in Pulka/ Gwoza

description.narrative: ltpgtNorwegian Church Aid (NCA) has been actively delivering integrated humanitarian assistance in northeast Nigeria since 2017, focusing on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), and Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV), and Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health (ASRH) across conflict-affected Local Government Areas （LGAs） in Borno State.ltbrgtThe proposed initiative is a multi-sectoral WASH/Protection （GBV） intervention designed to address critical gaps within Internally Displaced Persons （IDP） camps in Pulka. It aims to reach a total of 19,410 direct beneficiaries, including 7,963 women, 2,192 men, 6,440 girls, and 2,815 boys. lt/pgtltpgtAs part of the SGBV component, adolescent boys and girls will participate in life skills sessions called Enhancing Girls Agency and Gender Equality (ENGAGE) that tackle issues surrounding early and forced marriage. These sessions will incorporate strategies that promote education, awareness, and advocacy, alongside SGBV case management, and psychosocial support. Through structured curriculum families/ care givers, religious leaders, and communities will engage to challenge harmful social norms and foster supportive environments for adolescent development and access to sexual and reproductive health services.ltbrgtNCA will conduct integrated assessments to identify risks faced by women, girls, and persons with disabilities (PWDs), ensuring equitable access to WASH and healthcare services. WASH facilities will be strategically located to uphold the safety, dignity, and well-being of adolescent girls.ltbrgtNCA operates in two Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS) in Pulka and the SGBV intervention will also leverage these existing WGSS, specifically within transit Camp and camp D, to enhance timely access to lifesaving services. NCA will deliver holistic, survivor-centered SGBV response services, including case management and psychosocial support. NCA has been and will continue to enhancing through this project the Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) services in Pulka by collaborating with three local health facilities. This support includes capacity-building trainings for healthcare providers, in-kind contributions to strengthen facility operations, and targeted awareness campaigns that stress the urgency of reporting rape cases within 72 hours. The project will adopt the latest WHO guidelines on CMR and Intimate Partner Violence (IPV).ltbrgtIn addition to SGBV response services, the project will include awareness-raising, empowerment initiatives, and skills acquisition. Men will be engaged through a 12-week program, with weekly sessions of at least two hours, aimed at reducing and mitigating the impacts of SGBV-related issues. These sessions will address sexual violence, IPV, and Child, Early, and Forced Marriages (CEFM).ltbrgtTo promote menstrual hygiene and restore a sense of dignity among vulnerable women and girls in Pulka, NCA proposes the provision of dignity kits through targeted distributions. Each kit will contain essential hygiene items such as sanitary pads, underwear, soap, and other personal care products, designed to meet the immediate needs of most vulnerable women and girls. This intervention will be complemented by brief sensitization sessions on menstrual hygiene and self-care, contributing to improved health outcomes and psychosocial well-being. The activity will be implemented in coordination with local health facilities and community structures to ensure appropriate targeting and cultural relevance.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtIn the Wash sector, 15,000 IDPs will be reached with hygiene promotion, 3,750 with sanitation activities and, 5,000 for safe water access in Pulka to address critical gaps across all the camps. These gaps have been exacerbated by USAID funding cuts and the withdrawal of key actors. The project aims to contribute to reducing cholera risks by improving WASH services and ensuring their sustainability and effectiveness.lt/pgt
